title: Reinforcing Loops
hook: Happy customers bring in more customers, who bring in even more. That loop is worth more than any new idea.
statement: What grows, grows faster, as long as you keep feeding it.
explainer: Referrals, reviews, repeat buyers. These loops build on themselves. Feeding the one that's already working almost always beats starting something shiny and new.
sop: Find your strongest loop, like referrals, reviews, or repeat buyers.
Set the Base and Rate you're currently getting from it.
Remove one thing that's breaking its momentum.
Put more into this loop before starting a new one.
Track it monthly to confirm it's actually compounding.
equation_example: Base of 10 referral customers, Rate 20% a month, Time 6 months. 10 × 1.20 to the 6th power = about 30. A higher rate or more time means the loop is really taking off. A rate near zero means it's stalled.
question: Write down your strongest compounding loop and one way to feed it this week.
closing_statement: Feed what's already compounding before starting something new.
caption:
Principle Nº 121: Reinforcing Loops

Happy customers bring in more customers, who bring in even more. That loop is worth more than any new idea.

What grows, grows faster, as long as you keep feeding it.

Your turn: Write down your strongest compounding loop and one way to feed it this week.
